name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 486 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 43% more than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 486 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 43 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Armed men shot a Kuki civilian in Kangpokpi and villagers were killed in Khongbal Tangkhul, prompting protests in Manipur where effigies of the chief minister and deputy chief minister were burned and bodies of killed civilians were placed outside the chief minister’s residence, leading to calls for resignations. Police arrested multiple suspects in Manipur, seizing firearms and explosives after attacks in Nongshum, Khongban Sanurok, and a recent ambush in Kangpokpi, and detained three individuals during a combing operation in Kangpokpi. In Kashmir, the Northern Army commander reviewed security and operational preparedness while buses bound for the region were attacked in Punjab and Haryana, with passengers labeled terrorists. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Bevæpnede menn skjøt en Kuki-sivil i Kangpokpi, og landsbyboere ble drept i Khongbal Tangkhul, noe som førte til protester i Manipur hvor leirer av statsministeren og visestatsministeren ble brent og likene til drepte sivile ble plassert utenfor statsministerens bolig, med krav om avgang. Politiet arresterte flere mistenkte i Manipur, beslagla skytevåpen og sprengstoff etter angrep i Nongshum, Khongban Sanurok og et nylig bakholdsangrep i Kangpokpi, og holdt tre personer i varetekt under en gjennomgående operasjon i Kangpokpi. I Kashmir gjennomgikk den nordlige armékommandanten sikkerhets- og operasjonsberedskapen mens busser på vei til regionen ble angrepet i Punjab og Haryana, med passasjerer merket som terrorister. 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
